newsitem.title: CHINA: OLYMPICS-SAMARANCH CONFIRMS HONG KONG'S GAMES FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-SAMARANCH CONFIRMS HONG KONG'S GAMES FUTURE.

text.p: Hong Kong's continued participation in the Olympic Games was assured by International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Juan Antonio Samaranch on Thursday.
Just three days after China regained sovereignty over Hong Kong from Britain, the IOC chief said the former colony could continue to compete in the Olympic Games under their own flag.
Hong Kong won their first ever Olympic gold medal at last year's Games in Atlanta through women's windsurfer Lee Lai-shan.

Samaranch made the announcement in conjunction with the Amateur Sports Federation & Olympic Committee of Hong Kong (ASF&OC) after meeting Chinese Sports Minister Wu Shaozu and Hong Kong's new Chief Executive, Tung Chee-hwa.

"It is the common aim to enable the people of Hong Kong to continue taking part in the Olympic Games and generally in sports competitions everywhere as a separate and independent entity," Samaranch said in a statement.
"It is agreed therefore that the ASF&OC wlll retain its recognition as a National Olympic Committee and will function according to the Olympic Charter."

Samaranch confirmed that the ex-British territory would compete under the name "Hong Kong, China" and teams would fly the new Special Adminstrative Region (SAR) flag. He added that at flag-raising and victory ceremonies the Chinese National Anthem would be played.

Earlier in the day, Samaranch visited nearby Macau, which will revert to Chinese rule in 1999, and said he was hopeful the Portuguese enclave would be granted IOC membership before the end of the year.
"The process of the Macau Olympic Committee will be reassessed and we hope and wish that there will be good news for the territory within six months," he said.
